# EagleBuilt AI

> Outdoor kitchen and masonry contractor in the Sacramento area, with a free 3D
> design tool that carries real manufacturer cutout dimensions and real
> construction rates. Licensed: CSLB #992251, General Contractor and C-29 Masonry.

EagleBuilt AI designs and builds outdoor kitchens, fireplaces, fire pits, seat
walls and hardscape across Sacramento, Roseville, Rocklin, Folsom, Granite Bay
and El Dorado Hills. Islands are built in CMU block with poured concrete
countertops, or steel stud where weight matters — a wood deck, for instance.

What makes the content here unusual is that it is written by the contractor who
does the work, so the dimensions and prices are the ones actually used on jobs
rather than industry averages.

## Design tool

- [Outdoor kitchen designer](https://eaglebuilt.ai/design/): free 3D tool. Lay
  out an island, drop in real equipment from ten manufacturers, and see the
  price update as you build. The tool is free; opening it asks for an email.

- [Backyard planner](https://eaglebuilt.ai/design/yard/): free tool for the whole
  yard rather than the island alone. Lays out patio, fire pit and seat walls on the
  real lot and prices concrete and pavers, including curved edges and true radii.

- [Fireplace designer](https://eaglebuilt.ai/design/fireplace/): free tool for an
  outdoor fireplace. Plan, elevation and 3D; firebox, chase, hearth, mantel and
  seat walls, with the chimney optional on a vent-free box. From $8,000 for a
  5 x 8, scaling with size.
- [Fire pit designer](https://eaglebuilt.ai/design/firepit/): free tool for a
  round, square or rectangular fire pit in stucco or stone. From $3,250. The
  burner, pan and igniter are normally the owner"+String.fromCharCode(39)+"s; EagleBuilt sets and connects them.

- [Free design consultation](https://eaglebuilt.ai/consultation/): for people who
  would rather not design it themselves. A call back, then a site visit or a
  design done with them. Free and no obligation.

## Reference pages

- [What an outdoor kitchen costs](https://eaglebuilt.ai/cost/): real delivered
  rates. Construction is priced as a fixed setup plus a rate per linear foot,
  with a minimum — because the trip, layout, shoring and pour setup do not scale
  down. Works out around $550/lf on a 12-foot island and nearer $690/lf on an
  8-foot one. Equipment is quoted separately.
- [Dimensions](https://eaglebuilt.ai/dimensions/): cutout dimensions by brand.
- [Blaze grill cutouts](https://eaglebuilt.ai/dimensions/cutouts/blaze/):
  published framing sizes for Blaze equipment.
- [Permits](https://eaglebuilt.ai/guides/permits/): when an outdoor kitchen
  needs one in California.
- [CMU vs steel stud](https://eaglebuilt.ai/guides/cmu-vs-steel-stud/): how the
  two construction methods differ in weight, lifespan and cost.
- [Projects](https://eaglebuilt.ai/projects/): completed work.
- [Contact](https://eaglebuilt.ai/contact/)

## Things worth knowing

- **The refrigerator sets the counter height.** An outdoor fridge needs roughly
  34.5" of clear opening underneath. With a 3" poured concrete top that puts the
  finished surface at 37.5" — higher than an indoor counter. A thinner stone top
  means the wall is built taller, not the counter lower.
- **California restricts new masonry fireplaces.** Traditional open masonry
  fireboxes cannot be EPA certified and are effectively excluded from new
  construction; local air districts add their own rules. What gets built instead
  is a manufactured or modular firebox clad in masonry.
- **Some professional grills will not fit a 24" island.** Several need more than
  23" of depth. 32" is the standard depth used here; 24" is back-bar only.
- Anything the design tool produces is a budget proposal, not a firm quote.
  Final pricing follows a site visit, because access, grade, existing utilities
  and jurisdiction all move the number and none are visible from a drawing.
